claims.claim: JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported second-quarter 2026 net income of $21.2 billion.
Reported net income was $21.2 billion, or $7.70 per share.
Net income excluding significant items (non-GAAP) was $16.9 billion, or $6.14 per share.
Reported revenue was $57.3 billion.
Managed revenue (non-GAAP) was $58.0 billion.
Expense was $27.3 billion.
The reported overhead ratio was 48%.
The managed overhead ratio (non-GAAP) was 47%.
Credit costs were $2.5 billion.
Net charge-offs were $2.4 billion.
There was a $149 million net reserve build.
Reported Return on Equity (ROE) was 24%.
Return on Tangible Common Equity (ROTCE, non-GAAP) was 29%.
ROTCE excluding significant items (non-GAAP) was 23%.
CIB net income was $9.7 billion.
Markets revenue rose 35% year over year.
Equity Markets revenue was up 86%.
Fixed Income Markets revenue was up 6%.
Investment Banking fees increased 30% year over year.
CCB net income was $5.3 billion.
CCB revenue rose 8%.
Card Services & Auto net revenue was up 12% year over year.
The Card Services & Auto revenue increase was predominantly driven by higher net interest income on higher revolving balances.
AWM net income was $2.0 billion.
Assets under management (AUM) were $5.1 trillion, up 18% year over year.
The release provides no guidance or outlook.
The firm declared a common dividend of $4.0 billion, or $1.50 per share.
There were $6.2 billion of common stock net repurchases.
Basel III common equity Tier 1 capital was $303 billion.
The Basel III Standardized ratio was 14.1% and the Advanced ratio was 14.2%.
Cash and marketable securities were $1.5 trillion (estimated).
Average loans were $1.5 trillion.
Tangible book value per share (non-GAAP) was $113.35, up 10% year over year.
The CEO cited risks including geopolitical tensions, wars, sticky inflation, large global fiscal deficits and elevated asset prices, likened to shifting tectonic plates.
The Card Services net charge-off rate was 3.34% for the quarter.
Net interest income in Corporate decreased by $667 million this quarter, predominantly due to lower rates.
